artifacts.summary: Four-phase test-first plan: (1) author agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/tests/test-lean-sorry-census.sh with anti-vacuous dual assertions and prove it FAILS against the unfixed script; (2) swap line 144 to (?<![.\w])sorry\b and reconcile the two comment lines (11, 96) that name the old pattern, leaving line 5's rejected-grep-chain description and strip_lean_comments()'s body byte-identical; (3) real-corpus before/after differential over ~/Projects/cslib asserting delta == independently-grepped annotation count and no real sorry dropped, with --cross-check as the secondary oracle; (4) repo lint gates and source-store hygiene.

memory_candidates.content: Word-boundary regex bugs in census/count tooling are usually boundary-class bugs, not counting-logic bugs, and the two must be diagnosed separately. In Python/PCRE, \b fires between a word char and any non-word char including '.', so \bsorry\b matches inside dotted-qualified names like warn.sorry or foo.sorry. The fix is a negative lookbehind (?<![.\w])sorry\b, NOT a line-level pre-filter that skips lines containing the qualified name -- a skip-filter silently drops a real match riding on the same line as the annotation, converting an overcount into an undercount. Before changing such a matcher, determine whether the surrounding accumulator counts per-line (if re.search(line): total += 1) or per-occurrence (findall): a per-line accumulator makes same-line co-occurrence coincidentally correct today, so a well-intentioned switch to occurrence counting during the same edit reintroduces a double-count. Verification for this bug class must be differential and executed, never inspected: run the old and new matcher over the same real corpus and assert delta equals an independently-grepped count of the confounding token, plus that the post-fix inventory is a strict subset of the pre-fix one.
